sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Reply to Xin Li and Yapeng Xing's Letter to the Editor re: Nielsen N.K, Hjort P.B, Hansen E.B, et al. Substaging and stratified treatment of T1 bladder cancer - a nationwide register-based study. Eur Urol Open Sci 2026;90:92-100》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Body · p0010】We appreciate the authors for highlighting these methodological considerations, several of which also informed the interpretation and limitations of our study. As discussed in the article, treatment was guided by the substage under investigation, and the observed outcomes therefore reflect both tumor biology and management rather than the isolated effect of substaging. Accordingly, we stated that treatment selection limits causal interpretation. The recurrence and progression analyses were restricted to patients whose bladder was preserved, leaving a clinically selected pT1b population after 41% underwent early cystectomy; we acknowledged that this selection may exaggerate differences between pT1a and pT1b. Residual confounding from unavailable clinicopathological variables, including tumor size, multiplicity, concomitant carcinoma in situ, and lymphovascular invasion, was likewise described as a limitation.

【Body · p0015】Repeat resection is another important consideration. Repeat resection findings were unavailable in the registry, although a higher T1 substage recorded within 90 d resulted in reclassification, whereas ≥T2 disease identified within 90 d was considered initial understaging rather than progression. The 20% rate of muscle-invasive disease among patients with pT1b who underwent cystectomy therefore highlights a substantial risk of understaging. Detailed repeat-resection data would be important in future studies evaluating the independent value of pT1b for treatment selection.
